title: Co-Fermentation of Marsdenia tenacissima with Ganoderma lucidum and Anti-Lung Cancer Effect of the Fermentation Products
protocol: Extract MT with hot water (100 °C; MT/water = 1/10, w/v) for 30 min and collect the MT extraction residue as the test material.
Maintain LLC mouse lung cancer cell line in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 100 U/mL penicillin, and 100 μg/mL streptomycin in a humidified atmosphere at 37 °C under 5% CO2.
Keep C57BL/6J mice aged 6-8 weeks and weighing 19 ± 2 g in an environmentally controlled room with a 12 h/12 h light/dark cycle and unlimited access to food and water.
Disinfect the mice regularly.
Inoculate three strains of fungi into potato dextrose agar (PDA) solid medium using sterile techniques.
Culture the inoculated PDA dishes in the dark at 28 °C.
Store fully covered fungal cultures at 4 °C.
Inoculate strains preserved in PDA solid medium into seed solution of first-stage shake flask.
Culture inoculated strains at 28 °C, shaking at 120 rpm for 4-5 days.
Inoculate the first-stage fungi liquid into a shake flask containing secondary fungi liquid at a volume ratio of 1:20.
Culture secondary fungal liquid in constant temperature shaker for 4-5 days.
Dilute MT with water to 100 mg/L (MT/water).
Add diluted MT solution to agar to form solid medium.
Inoculate 1 mL of the secondary fungal liquid of each strain into the solid culture containing only MT.
Divide cultures into G. lucidum-MT, I. obliquus-MT, and O. sinensis-MT systems.
Place these culture systems at 28 °C without shaking in the dark.
Observe growth of strains in the three culture systems.
Select strains that can grow with MT for further screening.
Inoculate G. lucidum into liquid medium containing only MT for co-fermentation (MGF).
Inoculate O. sinensis into liquid medium containing only MT for co-fermentation (MOF).
Culture MGF and MOF in constant temperature shaker at 28 °C, shaking at 180 rpm for 10 days.
Filter mycelium through gauze after fermentation.
Dry the filtered mycelium.
Extract dried mycelium with 80% ethanol three times for 12 hours each.
Subcutaneously inject LLC cells (1.0 × 10^6 cells in 0.2 mL of PBS) into the right flank of male C57BL/6J mice.
Verify successful establishment of tumor model by checking for nodules approximately 5 mm in size.
Randomly group the tumor-bearing mice (n = 10 per group) into different treatment groups including control, model, MGF, MOF, MT, and cisplatin.
Administer saline to control and model groups.
Sacrifice the mice after 14 days of treatment.
Collect tumor tissue for analysis.
Extract 10 mg of MT, G. lucidum, and MT with G. lucidum co-fermentation (MGF) with 500 μL of methanol:H2O (7:3).
Shake the mixture at 4°C for 1 minute.
Sonicate the mixture for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,200 × g for 20 minutes.
Collect supernatants from the centrifuged mixture.
Filter the collected supernatants through a 0.22 μm polyvinylidene fluoride membrane.
Inject filtered samples into liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry setup (LC-MS/MS).
Dissolve the fermentation extract obtained from the fermentation broth in distilled water.
Stir the dissolved mixture thoroughly.
Repeat all fermentation experiments six times.
Assess statistical significance using Student's t-test.
Express all data as the mean ± SD.
Repeat all experiments in triplicate.
Set p < 0.05 for statistical significance.
Use SCIEX OS software to identify metabolites based on mass error, retention time, isotope match, MS/MS library purity score, and computational molecular formula.
Use a mass error < 5 ppm for identification.
Use an isotope ratio difference < 20 for identification.
Set the library score > 50 for identification.
